affected_system: privacy-preserving infectious-disease surveillance and response operations
alternatives: activate a bounded reserve from forecast risk bands for infectious-disease response workload
use rolling forecasts and conservative capacity triggers for infectious-disease response workload
pair reporting-delay-aware multistream demand forecasting with an explicit stop, review, and escalation rule
assumptions: Case, syndrome, testing, wastewater, vaccination, and care records have explicit definitions and delays.
No individual identity or protected health information enters public release artifacts.
All alternatives, capacities, costs, effects, thresholds, and failure scenarios are proposed until bound to evidence.
baseline: continue ordinary capacity planning for infectious-disease response workload.

constraints.description: The infectious-disease public-health operations forecast must respect declared validated operational capacity and forecast uncertainty.
Every released metric must retain evidence type, source lineage, geography, time, assumptions, and uncertainty.
No analytical output may bypass lawful authority, accountable human review, or an applicable appeal process.

decision_cadence: recompiled at each planning cycle and after material evidence change
decision_owner: communicable-disease director and public-health operations chief
decision_question: What probabilistic clinic, testing, laboratory, hotline, and bed demand should operations prepare for?

independence_key.binding_constraint: The infectious-disease public-health operations forecast must respect declared validated operational capacity and forecast uncertainty.
independence_key.evidence_gate: Evidence for infectious-disease response workload passes documented checks for held-out error, interval coverage, event detection, drift, and baseline comparison.
independence_key.primary_outcome: care and testing demand above staffed capacity

intended_claim: A versioned forecast design for comparing declared alternatives affecting infectious-disease response workload, conditional on its evidence gate.
limitations: This library record has no city binding and therefore reports no local input, output, or recommendation.
Readiness describes explicit source and method gates; it does not certify implementation feasibility.
External domain, legal, community, security, and operational review remains outside this design artifact.

objectives.metric: care and testing demand above staffed capacity
distributional gap in care and testing demand above staffed capacity
decision claims with complete evidence lineage

prohibited_claims: Do not call forecast workload infections, admissions, or transmission.
Do not describe a design-only record as a city execution, deployment, adopted policy, or impact result.
Do not relabel proposed, estimated, simulated, optimized, or causal evidence as observed evidence.
Do not infer individual behavior, protected status, harm, or entitlement from aggregate records.

release_gate.failure_release: Release an explicit insufficient-evidence record naming missing sources, failed diagnostics, prohibited claims, and the next validation action.
release_gate.pass_condition: Evidence for infectious-disease response workload passes documented checks for held-out error, interval coverage, event detection, drift, and baseline comparison.

title: Forecast infectious-disease care and testing demand
transportability_risks: Pathogens, immunity, clinical practice, reporting, testing, and public behavior differ.
Surveillance changes can mimic epidemiological changes.
